content.title: Stock Market News, April 10, 2026: Dow Falls After Highest Inflation Reading Since 2024
content.text:
Asia Dow5761.34-0.77%Nikkei58952.11-1.06%Hang Seng25914.66-0.95%Shanghai4092.02-0.35%BSE Sensex78516.49-0.95%Singapore4954.70-0.96%Kospi6429.380.18%ASX-2008775.50-0.77% Markets CoverageThe latest news & analysisAcross the MarketsEconomyStreetwiseStocksQuick TakesMarket DataYour MoneyNewsletter SignupUpdated April 10, 2026 at 8:40pm ETStock Market News, April 10, 2026: Dow Falls After Highest Inflation Reading Since 2024Nasdaq rises, bond yields edge higher after CPI matches expectations

The Dow industrials ended a strong week on a down note after inflation came in at its highest level in nearly two years.The March CPI report showed prices rose 0.9% from a month earlier and 3.3% from a year earlier—the largest annual increase since May 2024.U.S. stocks finished Friday mixed, with the Dow falling about 0.6%, or 269 points, and the the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite up 0.4%. The S&P 500, which fell 0.1%, and the other benchmarks were up 3% or more for the week, their biggest gains since November.With consumer prices, nearly three-quarters of the monthly increase was driven by higher gasoline prices. Food inflation came in lower, and overall, the readings were in line with economists’ expectations.Consumer sentiment meanwhile fell in April to the lowest level in the history of the University of Michigan survey, showing Americans' heightened concerns about the Iran war hitting the domestic economy.U.S. oil prices slipped 1.3% to $96.57 a barrel. For the week, they tumbled 13% in their biggest weekly decline since 2020.With the U.S.-Iran cease-fire remaining on shaky ground, traders are also closely watching for updates in the Middle East. Talks between Tehran and Washington are scheduled for Saturday in Islamabad, though Iranian officials have said publicly their attendance is contingent on the situation in Lebanon.European stocks wrapped up the week on a positive note, following most Asian indexes. Treasury yields edged higher, while the WSJ Dollar Index slipped.🔎 Check out the weekly markets roundup or listen to the WSJ Minute Briefing podcast. Also follow our live Middle East updates.— By Caitlin McCabe
